Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Digital revenue collection is supported through government e-services and payment integrations (eCitizen accepts digital payments for government services; PesaLink integration supports payments for government fees). This supports at least partial digital revenue collection.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: KRA's own channels (iTax, Lipa Ushuru na M-Pesa paybills 222222/572572, and the eCustoms app) show individual income tax, PAYE, corporation tax, VAT and customs duties are all payable digitally via mobile money, card or bank, current as of 2025-26 — broader coverage than the single Pesalink source originally cited. Raised from Partial (2) to Yes (3) as most major tax types are digitally payable, not just select fees.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: Kenya uses digital channels for G2P social transfers: the government’s Inua Jamii cash transfer programme has been transitioning payments via eCitizen to M‑Pesa agents (mobile payments) to make access easier through the wide network of M‑PESA agents.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The official mygov.go.ke article (Feb 2025) and CBK's National Payments System Vision & Strategy corroborate active G2P use: Inua Jamii cash transfers (KES 3.52bn to 1.76m beneficiaries for the January 2025 cycle) are disbursed via M-Pesa/eCitizen, building on a 2013 presidential directive digitising all government payments. Score of 3 (Yes - Active Use) confirmed; no change.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: P2B/merchant payments are widely available via mobile money (e.g., Lipa na M‑PESA “Buy Goods”/merchant till and paybill), and CBK launched mobile money merchant interoperability in 2022 to allow customers to pay merchants across networks.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed by re-reading the original CBK press release (8 April 2022, an authoritative regulator source): mobile money merchant interoperability across Safaricom, Airtel and Telkom enables P2B payments to any merchant regardless of network. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed; no change, though note this is a 2022 launch date and no fresher adoption/coverage figures were independently found.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: P2G payments are supported through eCitizen integrations and mobile money rails: PesaLink is integrated with Kenya’s eCitizen platform, enabling citizens to pay for government services (licenses, passports, business registration fees) via instant payments.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Pesalink's own product page confirms eCitizen integration for licenses, passports and business registration fees, and KRA confirms taxes are payable via M-Pesa paybill/iTax. Score of 3 (Yes - Active Use) confirmed; no change.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: PesaLink has documented scheme rules: AfricaNenda reports IPSL launched PesaLink scheme rules in 2022, covering member obligations, governance framework, operating model, transaction flows, and penalties. However, a publicly accessible full rulebook was not found on the operator website during research, so rules appear only partially publicly available (e.g., referenced in reports or accessible to participants).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. AfricaNenda's SIIPS 2022 case study describes PesaLink's scheme rules (member obligations, governance framework, penalties) in detail, but no downloadable rulebook was found; Pesalink's own FAQ/resource-centre pages contain only general product information, not the rules themselves. Score of 2 (Partial - On Request) confirmed; no change.
